name: Rasalas
description: A star 38 parsecs away, 12 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48455: radius 11.79 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 51.395 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.056) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48455: effective temperature 4504 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.077)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48455: distance 38.052 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.006), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 38 parsecs away, 12 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 51 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,504 K, so 11.79 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 48455: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Mu Leonis
quotes.card: Mu Leonis, also named Rasalas, is a star in the equatorial-northern constellation of Leo.
quotes.introduction: The apparent visual magnitude of this star is 3.88, which is bright enough to be seen with the naked eye.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 643819484617141504 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
